source.paper: Hashimoto & Ohgushi (2023) Ecology and Evolution, doi:10.1002/ece3.10164
past_studies: Hashimoto & Ohgushi 2017, Population Ecology, doi:10.1007/s10144-016-0568-8, regrowth and repeated herbivory
Hashimoto & Ohgushi 2023, Ecol Evol, doi:10.1002/ece3.10164, competitor density, 2.6x food demand and asymmetric survival
Hashimoto & Ohgushi 2012 ESJ59 poster, temporal/spatial plant regeneration already hypothesized

distinct_hypothesis: At equal total supplied edible host biomass, does timing of plant regrowth (resource continuity versus an early or late pulse) modify or reverse the asymmetric effect of one butterfly species on the other's successfully emerged adult offspring?

required: two-species starting larval densities per cage
Final four plant-individual ordinal remaining-food bins interpreted at one endpoint, not longitudinal biomass
Original 15 initial density combinations × exactly two cage replicates
interpretation: If repeated biomass curves exist without randomized timing, source supports only descriptive feasibility, not causal manipulation of resource pulses
If stage-specific larval survival is observed, time-specific correlation with regrowth remains potential reverse causation because food demand causes defoliation
A plant-accessory effect by species identity is prior art and cannot be called new
No independent plant regrowth timing is measured or manipulated; previous notes referring to four defoliation timepoints were erroneous.
preexisting_data_gate.source_stop: Without random or quasi-exogenous regrowth timing with matched cumulative edible biomass, do not infer plant temporal compensation as causal competition mechanism from reanalysis.
preexisting_data_gate.original_plant_table_semantics: 30 cages with four FINAL plant-individual categories; NO time-stamped plant regrowth or randomized regrowth pulse treatment.

future_experiment.design: 2 focal butterfly species × species-specific competitor presence/density × plant supply timing under matched total edible biomass, with predeclared pulse regime and alternative continuous-supply/sham handling controls
future_experiment.response: flight-capable adult production and developmental time per original focal cohort, including deaths and pupal failure
future_experiment.replicate: independently randomized plant/enclosure, with populations/years and maternal families separately represented
future_experiment.mechanism: Disentangle regrowth/leaf age/plant quality from amount; experimental timing effect ≠ introduced-plant origin
future_experiment.novelty: A dynamic interaction-mediated butterfly effect at equal season-total edible host resource would differ from 2017 host regrowth and 2023 static competitor density studies, if genuinely independent manipulation and replication demonstrate it.

source_data_correction: 2023 defoliation.1–4 are four individual potted host plants within each cage at one FINAL measurement, not four sampling times. Values are visually scored ordinal food-remaining bands, not measured biomass. The 690 larval observations are longitudinal, plant food supply is not.
original_2012_prior_art: ESJ59 poster P1-196A (Hashimoto & Ohgushi) already explicitly hypothesized that spatial and temporal regeneration of A. debilis relaxes competition. A timing-only study cannot claim to have originated that ecological idea.
novelty_priority: The non-food-shortage heterospecific suppression identified in the 2023 paper is a narrower causal-mechanism gap: discriminate plant-quality induction, mechanical wounding, donor residues and direct interference at equal edible host biomass.
